answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents named nectar, walnut, and sparrow each face the same rule; creating more names does not bypass it. An attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full period, paying financing costs and forgoing other uses of that capital. This makes a swarm costly, though a wealthy attacker can still fund one.
